spots.line: The hut is half a hut. The other half is the rockfall it was built against.
A cairn, and then another, and they go up the slope out of sight.
Tools laid out by size. Every one of them for working stone.
Chips of stone underfoot everywhere, in a country with no quarry.

chests.line: A niche in the fall with a flat stone over it, and the stone lifts.

people.name: Durn the Cairnwright
chatter: One stone a day. Some days two. I am not in a hurry and neither are they.
The fall came down before my grandfather. The hut came after. That is the whole story.
Every cairn is somebody. I do not always know which somebody.
You can sleep here. Do not sleep under the fall.

people.name: a bear that has claimed the slope
chatter: It is stood on something it should not be able to stand on.
